CanonicalVars.rationale: All four vars ported: `DamageVar(5m, Move)`, `RepeatVar(2)`, `PowerVar<StrengthPower>(3m)` and `DynamicVar("EnemyStrength", 1m)` (FightMe.cs:20-26). `base_hits` reports 2 and `magic_number` reports the self-Strength 3. One of the few multi-var cards in the pool with NO inlined number.

OnPlay.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): The enemy-side Strength is unguarded now, exactly like the SELF Strength on the line above it (FightMe.cs:40-41). The card's own `if not target.is_gone:` is DELETED and PowerCmd.apply now carries the WHOLE of `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-322): `cmds.can_receive_powers` is `not target.is_removed_from_combat and hooks.should_allow_hitting(target)`, and `Creature.is_removed_from_combat` (creatures.py) is `is_gone and not retained_after_death` -- the sim's expression of `CombatState == null`, since it never drops a corpse from `enemies` (conformance addresses enemies by index). The two edits are a MATCHED PAIR: round 6 had wired only the ShouldAllowHitting half here, so deleting the card guard on its own would have powered the ordinary corpse that CreatureCmd.cs:523-531 removes. Pinned by test/test_can_receive_powers.py -- ordinary corpse refused, removal-vetoed corpse powered, mid-revival corpse still refused. The per-hit `if target.is_gone or ctx.player.is_dead: break` STAYS: that one is AttackCommand's own, which breaks on `Attacker.IsDead` and on an empty `validTargets` filtered by `IsAlive` (AttackCommand.cs:538-550). WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE: the observable the entry proposed -- a Vicious draw off a retained corpse -- is not reachable in the sim's SHIPPED content, and the enumeration is the finding. Every sim producer of a retained corpse also makes it unhittable for as long as it lasts (IllusionPower.cs:95-105, AdaptablePower.cs:68-78 and ReattachPower.cs:74-86 each pair the removal veto with ShouldAllowHitting), the sole exception being a Decimillipede segment killed with every other segment already down -- and that ends the combat, so PowerCmd.Apply's own IsEnding guard (PowerCmd.cs:69-72) swallows it first. The game's third case, PainfulStabsPower.cs:29-32 on Test Subject phase 2, retains WITHOUT vetoing hits and the sim's PainfulStabsPower omits that override; recorded here rather than fixed, because it is not this entry's line. The code is now the source's shape either way.  The text it replaced read: The attack (5 damage, 2 hits), the self-Strength 3 and the enemy-Strength 1 are all faithful and in C#'s order: attack, then SELF, then TARGET (FightMe.cs:36-41). The divergence is the sim's extra `if not target.is_gone:` before the enemy's Strength (fight_me.py:45-46). C# applies the power unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse (`CombatState == null`). The two agree for an ordinary kill, because `CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `await Kill(...)` before returning (CreatureCmd.cs:409) and removal happens at CreatureCmd.cs:523-525. They diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower and any other listener that fires on a power landing regardless of target liveness. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. EXECUTED: `py audit/tools/card_probes.py dead-target-guards` lists 41 sim card classes that test liveness. Note the SELF Strength is correctly unguarded on both sides, so only the enemy half diverges.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` + `DynamicVars.Strength.UpgradeValueBy(1m)` (FightMe.cs:46-47) == `_damage += 1` (5 -> 6) and `_strength += 1` (3 -> 4). The REPEAT stays 2 and the ENEMY Strength stays 1 when upgraded on both sides -- all four upgraded numbers checked, and the two that do NOT change are the easy ones to get wrong.

guards.what: the sim routes BOTH Strength applications through `StrengthCmd.apply`, which runs `hooks.modify_strength_given` first (cmds.py:349-361); C# calls `PowerCmd.Apply<StrengthPower>` directly at both sites (FightMe.cs:40-41)
guards.rationale: For the SELF application the two agree in effect -- C#'s `Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven` / `...Received` chain is the engine-level equivalent and is power_cmd seam territory. For the ENEMY application the sim additionally runs the player's strength-given modifiers over a buff the ENEMY receives, which C# would also do via ModifyPowerAmountGiven since the applier is the player either way. Recorded as a deliberate divergence rather than a gap because the sim's StrengthCmd is a documented re-architecture of the same modifier chain and no ported `modify_strength_given` listener distinguishes the two targets; if one is ported that keys on the RECIPIENT, this becomes a gap.
